title: Static Sword Leaf Upright and Reflexed Iris
description: One newly authored complete stylised above-ground iris-like flowering plant. A small basal crown supports a fan of long flattened sword leaves and one narrow gently bent stalk. The upright flower has three thick broad inward-arching upper petals alternating with three broad outward-then-downward reflexed falls, each a continuous curved finite-thickness volume; the falls carry a small integral yellow face region near their roots. This alternating high enclosing and low drooping organisation differs from a front-facing orchid lower lip and the central trumpet of a daffodil, not merely a different petal count or color. All leaf and petal sections, paths and crown placement are newly drawn. One static whole plant zero scenes. Roots, exact species, reproductive microanatomy, growth, pollination, cultivation, ecological function, wind, animation and interaction are not made or validated.
